scenes.heading: Writing a returns and refunds policy that protects you

sents.d: Writing a returns and refunds policy that protects you
A vague or missing returns policy costs you more in disputes than a clear, slightly strict one ever will.

scenes.heading: Write it before your first sale

sents.d: A written returns policy — window length, condition requirements, who pays return shipping, refund vs. store credit — needs to exist before your first sale, not after your first dispute, since platforms and payment processors often default to the buyer's favor when no clear policy was stated upfront.
Being reasonably generous on window length but specific on condition requirements (unworn, original packaging, etc.) balances customer trust against restocking losses better than either extreme.

Displaying the policy clearly at checkout, not just buried in a footer link, actually reduces disputes — customers who know the terms upfront are less likely to open a dispute instead of a normal return.

take: Publish a clear returns policy and show it at checkout.
